mutants.reason: Inverting w_req_event makes the completer FSM leave IDLE when there is no request and ignore a real one, so PSEL rises with no Setup and requested transfers are lost.
The async reset value of o_apb_pwakeup becomes 1, so it is high during slv reset and, in APB4, stays 1 until the first clock edge after reset release, instead of 0.

The delay model updates its output only when the stage input is unchanged, so with the model enabled a real toggle of req/ack is no longer picked up as a change and crossings are lost or wrongly delayed, hanging the transfer.
When extra latency is drawn, the pending flag is never set, so the delayed value is never applied to sim_cur and the req/ack crossing is stuck and the transfer never completes.

In APB5 the wake-up sampling is inverted: reg_wakeup is 0 when the APB5 parameter is 1, so i_apb_pwakeup is never forwarded to o_apb_pwakeup. The sync of the requester wake-up is lost; only the in-progress term remains.

The reset value of the pending flag becomes 1, so after reset release the model loads the uninitialised sim_nxt into sim_cur, giving X or a spurious request/ack on the sync output and a spurious transfer or X after reset.

The extra-latency counter test is inverted: an extra delay of 1 is applied one cycle late and an extra delay of 2 is applied one cycle early, so the random crossing latency changes cycle by cycle but stays within the allowed window, which is why no check kills it.
The mst reset condition is inverted, so req, wakeup and pready are held at 0 while the reset is released and load their next-state values while it is asserted, and no transfer can complete.
The APB5 enable is inverted, so in the APB4 configuration o_apb_pwakeup follows the wake-up/in-progress terms instead of being 0, and in APB5 it would stay 0 so PWAKEUP is missing at PSEL.

In the two-phase handshake ack is set to 1 instead of toggled, so the first acknowledge works but later ones produce no toggle, so later transfers never receive PREADY (and with 4-phase it would toggle wrongly).

In the synthesis cell the reset value of the chain is 1, so req or ack synchronizer outputs are 1 during and after reset, causing a spurious request or acknowledge and a phantom transfer or PREADY after reset release.
The cell reset condition is inverted, so the chain is cleared while RN is high and shifts only while RN is low, so Q stays 0 in normal operation and no crossing ever arrives.
